 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Karthik V., who is son of petitioner, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 13-10-2023 at about 8.15 p.m., the deceased Karthik V. and his friends Nanda Kumar and Chandan Kumar were going to college on Pro Passion bike bearing No.KA-53-V- 9836.

Karthik and Chandan Kumar were pillion riders and Nanda Kumar was riding the said vehicle on Vijayapura road, Shidlaghatta Taluk, slowly,
cautiously, by observing all the traffic norms and regulations.

When they reached near Shrushti Hospital, H-Cross, on Vijayapura road, at that time a Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209, which was going ahead of their two-wheeler,
driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, suddenly took right turn and hit the two-wheeler.

At the same time, a KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 which was coming from H-Cross, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, without observing any traffic norms and regulations, endangering to human life and dashed against the said two- wheeler.
Due to the said impact, the rider and pillion riders along with the bike fell down.
The said bus dragged the deceased Karthik by its front wheel to some extent.
Consequently, Karthik sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to MVJ Hospital, Hoskote, wherein the duty doctors examined him and declared brought dead.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was final year B.Com student.
He was the last hope of the petitioner and he had very bright future.
The petitioner was dependent upon him for her future life.
She is under mental shock due to sudden demise of her only son.
She lost his love and affection, now her life has become dark and miserable.

The Shidlagatta Rural Police have registered the case against the drivers of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F- 0869 and Omni car/van bearing No.KA-01-MD-8209, for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A)

The respondent No.1 is the owner of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-0869 and respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the Omni car/van bearing No.KA-01-MD-8209.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for mis-joinder of parties.

For the alleged accident, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V-9836 and the driver of the Maruthi van bearing No.KA-01-MD-8209 were wholly and solely responsible and consequently the owner and insurer of the motorcycle are the necessary parties to the present case.
But they are not made as parties to the petition.
On the contrary, the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-40-F-0869 was no way responsible for the alleged accident and consequently this respondent is not a necessary party.

But,
it has been made party with ulterior intention.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident, the bus in question was on its schedule trip from H-Cross to Chikkaballapura and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly, cautiously, on the left side of the road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

While it was so proceeding near Shrusti Hospital on H-Cross and Vijayapura road, at that time the Maruthi van bearing No.KA-01-MD-8209 was coming from the opposite side, being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with terrific speed and behind the said Maruthi van, the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V- 9836 was coming, being ridden by its rider along with two pillion riders, without wearing the head gears, in rash and negligent manner,
with high speed, in a zig zag manner, trying to overtake the Maruthi van.
But, the driver of the Maruthi van to avoid the overtaking took his vehicle towards right side.

As the motorcycle and van were being driven at high speed, there was a terrific collusion between the said vehicles and the occupants of the motorcycle were thrown out from the motorcycle and one among them i.e.
deceased fell down on the path to the bus.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas the respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made against it in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Omni car bearing No.KA-01-MD-0869 in favour of respondent No.2 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It has contended that, the driver of the Omni car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 149 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the deceased and also involvement of the Omni car in the alleged accident.

Further it is contended that,
the accident in question has not occurred on account of the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle.

The said vehicle was driven by it slowly, carefully and cautiously, on the correct side of the Padma Alias Padmamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51046653/

Further, in support of her oral evidence, the she has got marked total 28 documents as Ex.P.1 to 28.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 is true copy of first information statement, Ex.P.3 is true copy of spot mahazer, Ex.P.4 to 6 are true copy of seizure mahazer (total 3),

13. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 17, prima-facia it reveals that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209.

The said accident has taken place due to dashing of Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 to the ongoing motorcycle of the deceased and due to said impact the rider, deceased and another pillion rider fell down on the road.

At that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869,
which was coming from H-Cross with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased Karthik and dragged him by its front wheel to some extent.
Due to which the deceased Karthik has sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the said injuries.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.15, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 and deceased Karthik has succumbed to the grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
14.

At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MD-8209 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy in favour of the respondent No.2, with respect to offending Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the owner of offending Maruti Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 i.e. respondent No.2, as he did not choose to appear and file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 owner of the KSRTC bus and respondent No.3/insurer of Omni car/van, have specifically denied the Padma Alias Padmamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51046653/
6 above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, there is no negligence on the part of their respective drivers and the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the motorcycle.

sentences.text:
Further, the respondent No.1 has contended that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle and Maruthi Van, as the motorcycle rider was ridden along with two pillion riders,
without wearing head gears, in rash and negligent manner, with high speed, in a zigzag manner and while he was trying to overtake the Maruthi van, the driver of said Maruthi van in order to avoid the overtaking took his vehicle to the right side and as the motorcycle and van were at high speed, there was a terrific collusion between the motorcycle and the van.
The occupants of the motorcycle were thrown out from the motorcycle and one among them i.e. deceased fell down on the path of the bus and sustained grievous injuries and died.

Whereas, the respondent No.3 has contended that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V-9836 and KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 0869 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of Maruti Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209.
But, the respondent No.1 & 3 have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the driver of KSRTC bus and R.W.2, who is the representative/Legal Manager of respondent No.3 insurance company, there is absolutely no other independent corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 & 3 to establish the above contentions.

There is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing bearing No.KA-53-V-9836, on which the deceased was traveling as a pillion rider or there was any contributory negligence on his part.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 and the deceased Karthik V., has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.1 and 3 have cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence.

Further, the P.W.1 has unequivocally denied the suggestions made in her cross- examination that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle, as he was without observing the movement of the vehicles suddenly overtook Omni car/van and when he saw the vehicle coming from opposite side, he was unable to control his vehicle and fell down from the two-wheeler and came under the KSRTC bus wheel,
sustained grievous injuries and died.
15.

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.7 sketch clearly goes to show that, the said accident has taken place on the extreme left side of 22 feet wide Chikkaballapura-H Cross - Kolar SH-96,
infront of Devarajappa land, Kambiganahalli Village, Shidlaghatta Taluk, Chikkaballapura District,
due to dashing of offending Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 to the motorcycle of the deceased and due to ran over of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 0869 over the body of deceased.
Further it is pertinent to note, as per Ex.P.13 Motor Vehicle Accident Report, the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the offending vehicles and there was no rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the motorcycle of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred Padma Alias Padmamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51046653/
7

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents No.1 and 3 to disprove the case of the petitioners to show that, the said accident has taken place due to sole rash and negligent riding of the deceased and there was no fault on the part of the drivers of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209.

Even nothing has been brought out in the cross-examination of P.W.1 to show that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle of the deceased or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

16. Further, the Ex.P.14 Post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Karthik V., has died due to haemorrhage and shock due to polytrauma and intraabdominal injury sustained in the road traffic accident.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.15, has clearly stated that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the drivers of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MD-8209.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owners or by the drivers of the offending KSRTC Bus and Omni car/van.

In such circumstances,
there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, with regard to date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 and Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the drivers of offending vehicles, injuries caused to deceased Karthik V., in the said accident and the cause of his death.
17. But, it is pertinent to note that, admittedly, at the time of accident the deceased and two others were triple riders on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V-9836.

This clearly goes to show that, the deceased consciously and being fully aware that, triple riding is not allowed and it amounts to violation of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act and it may lead the rider to lose control over the said vehicle due to congestion, has taken risk of traveling on the said motorcycle as a pillion rider.
No doubt, mere act of triple riding does not amount to contributory negligence.
But, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case the pillion riders were not the children, but, they are young and healthy persons, both aged about 21 years and 20 years respectively.

In such circumstances, there are every chances that, due to triple riding on the motorcycle by the deceased, which is meant for two persons, there would have been congestion to the rider of motorcycle and he might have lost control and contributed in the cause of accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the very act of triple riding by the deceased has also contributed in the cause of accident to some extent.

But,
as there is no cogent and corroborative evidence to show that, the very act of triple riding has contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon the victim, this Court is of the opinion that, holding the deceased is liable for contributory negligence to the extent of 10%
would meet the ends of justice.

18. Further, the evidence on record clearly establishes that, there is equal contributory negligence on the part of the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 0869 and driver of Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD- 8209 in the cause of accident.

If the driver of offending Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 had taken care and if he had not driven his vehicle in rash Padma Alias Padmamma vs K.S.R.T.C on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51046653/

8 and negligent manner, the said car would not have come in contact with the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V-9836 of and the deceased would not have fell down from the said motorcycle and the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 would not have ran over his body.

Likewise, if the driver of offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 had been diligent and drove his vehicle in moderate speed, he would have immediately stopped his vehicle by applying break and the said vehicle would not dragged the body of the deceased Karthik to some extent and it had not ran over his body and resulted in his death.

But, the driver of offending Omni car/van bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-MD-8209 was the root cause to the accident.

If he had not dashed the motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-V-9836, the deceased would not have fell down from the said motorcycle and the offending KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F-0869 would not have ran over his body.

Therefore,
this Court is of the opinion that, the driver of Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA- 01-MD-8209 has contributed more in the cause of accident, as such he is to be held more responsible for the said accident, than the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA- 40-F-0869.

Accordingly, holding that,
the driver of Omni car/van bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MD-8209 has contributed 60% and the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg. No.KA-40-F- 0869 has contributed 30% and the deceased has contributed 10% in the cause of accident
, will be justifiable and would meet the ends of justice.

19. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

21. Therefore, in the light of observations made in the above cited decisions and for the reasons stated above, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioner has successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased Karthik V., has succumbed to the injuries sustained in motor vehicle accident, occurred on 13-10-2023 at about 8.15 p.m., on Chikkaballapura-H Cross - Kolar SH-96, in front of Devarajappa land, Kambiganahalli Village,

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major, married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
